issues_in.problem: 把使者之辞概括为「魏国答应的救兵至今不到」，原文重心是「今邯鄲旦暮降秦而魏救不至」——邯郸旦暮降秦这一层被抹去
issues_in.suggestion: 补上「邯郸旦暮之间就要降秦，而魏国救兵不至」

issues_in.problem: 「魏王不肯再发兵」证据包无（虽标简报转述）；「手里只有三千门客，没有兵权」中「没有兵权」是推断，证据只说「不敢任公子以國政」；「拼个同归于尽」超出 E13「欲死秦軍」的记述，添了意图
issues_in.suggestion: 改为「魏王未再发兵（据简报转述），公子手中只有门客，无国政之任；他决意赴秦军而死」

issues_in.problem: 「他连调动一支偏师的资格都没有，手里只剩人，没有权」写成事实，证据（SJ0771-E3）只有「不敢任公子以國政」，具体到「偏师」是作者外推
issues_in.suggestion: 改为「他未被任以国政，调兵无从谈起（作者推断）」

issues_in.problem: 把公子出口之言改写成内心活动：原文是「公子……心不快，曰：『吾所以待侯生者備矣……』」，稿件写成「想的是自己待侯生不薄……」；且「心不快」是司马迁叙述用语，稿件既承认是叙述用语，又把其后自言当心理实录
issues_in.suggestion: 改为「心不快，说：『吾所以待侯生者備矣……我豈有所失哉？』」

issues_in.problem: 「这场救赵从头到尾没有魏王的授权」与证据矛盾：E9 明载魏王遣晋鄙将十万众救赵，最初是奉王命出兵，无授权的只是矫符夺军、杀将
issues_in.suggestion: 改为「夺军救赵这一段没有魏王的授权」，删「从头到尾」

issues_in.problem: 「如侯嬴屏人间语献计」是证据包没有的细节：E15 未记「屏人」「间语」，且《史记》中「屏人間語」是公子屏退左右问计的行为，此处把细节和归属都安到侯嬴头上
issues_in.suggestion: 删去「屏人间语」，改为「如侯嬴献窃符之计、朱亥答话，是史家的记述，未必逐字」

issues_in.problem: English adds a fact not in the Chinese: "from the king on down no one could get it for her" (i.e., the king and all below tried and failed to avenge her father). The Chinese only says she was unable to take revenge for three years.
issues_in.suggestion: Delete "and from the king on down no one could get it for her", or add the equivalent to the Chinese line.

issues_in.problem: English adds the place name "at Ye" ("hold the army at Ye in wait-and-see"); the Chinese only says 魏王使人止晋鄙留军观望 with no location.
issues_in.suggestion: Drop "at Ye", or add 驻于邺 (or 邺) to the Chinese.

edits_applied.before: 魏安釐王二十年，秦军在长平歼灭赵军主力之后，进兵围住邯郸。魏王派将军晋鄙带十万众救赵，大军却没有走到邯郸（据简报转述）——平原君的使者一批批赶到大梁，车盖接连不断，话一句比一句重：魏国答应的救兵至今不到，公子不是自命能急人之困吗？末了还添一句「獨不憐公子姊邪」。公子无忌的姐姐，正是平原君夫人。
edits_applied.after: 魏安釐王二十年，秦军在长平歼灭赵军主力之后，进兵围住邯郸。魏王派将军晋鄙带十万众救赵，大军却没有走到邯郸（据简报转述）——平原君的使者一批批赶到大梁，车盖接连不断，话一句比一句重：邯郸旦暮之间就要降秦，而魏国答应的救兵至今不到，公子不是自命能急人之困吗？末了还添一句「獨不憐公子姊邪」。公子无忌的姐姐，正是平原君夫人。
edits_applied.reason: 补回 E11「今邯鄲旦暮降秦而魏救不至」中被抹去的“邯郸旦暮降秦”一层，保持使者原话的重心。

edits_applied.before: In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, after Qin had annihilated Zhao's main force at Changping, its armies pressed on and encircled Handan. The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao, but the army never reached the city (retold from the briefing). Instead, envoys from Lord Pingyuan arrived in Daliang one after another — caps of office and carriage canopies in an unbroken line — each message harsher than the last: the relief Wei had promised still had not come, and was Lord Xinling not the man who prided himself on rushing to others in distress? The last message added a barb: "And have you no pity for your own sister?" Lord Xinling's elder sister was Lord Pingyuan's wife.

The last message added a barb: "And have you no pity for your own sister?" Lord Xinling's elder sister was Lord Pingyuan's wife.
edits_applied.reason: 与中文同步补入 E11「今邯鄲旦暮降秦而魏救不至」的邯郸旦暮降秦一层。

edits_applied.before: Read the episode both ways. His intelligence was proven — and the price went straight onto the ledger: "From then on the king of Wei feared Lord Xinling's ability and dared not entrust him with the government of the state." The more capable he appeared, the less his king would hand him. By the time Handan cried for help he could not command even a detachment: plenty of people, no authority at all.

edits_applied.before: 那天他出城，路过夷门，见到侯生，把要去秦军送死的打算讲了，辞决而行。侯生只说一句「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」。车行数里，公子心不快——这是《史记》的叙述用语——想的是自己待侯生不薄，天下莫不闻，如今将死，对方竟无一言半辞相送。他「復引車還，問侯生」。

edits_applied.before: That day he rode out, passed the Yimen gate, stopped to see Hou Ying and told him the whole plan — going to die at the Qin army — then took his leave and set off. Hou Ying said only: "Push on, my lord; this old servant cannot follow you." A few li on, the lord felt a gnawing unhappiness — the narrator's own phrase — reasoning that he had treated Hou Ying handsomely, as all the world knew, and now, going to his death, the old man had not half a word to see him off. Had he fallen short somewhere? So he "turned his carriage around and went back to question Hou Ying."

edits_applied.before: Start with the sources. This piece rests on a single one: one account in the "Hereditary House of Lord Wei" in the Records of the Grand Historian, with no corroboration to set against it. The whispered schemes and dialogue — Hou Ying's secret counsel, Zhu Hai's reply — are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim. The lord's "unease," "self-congratulation," and "blaming himself" are narrative labels, not recorded psychology. The year is given as the twentieth of King Anxi of Wei, as the source has it, with no conversion to the common era.

edits_applied.before: Hou Ying's plan: the tally that authorized Jin Bi to move troops — a tiger tally — was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber, and Lady Ruji, the king's favorite, came and went there and was able to steal it. Her father had been murdered; for three years she had sought revenge, and from the king on down no one could get it for her. She had wept to Lord Xinling, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and presented it to her respectfully. The source has her ready to die for Lord Xinling and to refuse him nothing; only "she had no way to repay him." If the lord would but ask, she would certainly agree. Then, with the tiger tally in hand, seize Jin Bi's army, relieve Zhao in the north and drive Qin back in the west: "that is an achievement to rank with the Five Hegemons."

edits_applied.before: The detail most worth doubting: the figure of "eighty thousand picked men" appears here alone, with no corroboration; how the tallies were verified in Jin Bi's camp and how the affair wound up after the killing of the general go unrecorded; Hou Ying's motive in cutting his own throat, and Lady Ruji's fate after stealing the tally, come down to an act and a single sentence, with nothing further. issues.problem: English adds details absent from Chinese: "the eastern gate of Daliang" (ZH only says 夷门 / 大梁夷门), "called on him" before the gift, "when everyone was seated", and "with his carriage and escort".
issues.suggestion: Trim to the Chinese scope, e.g. "kept the Yimen, a gate of Daliang" and "wanted to make him a handsome gift".

issues.problem: The causal 以致 ("so that / resulting in") before 食客三千人 is rendered as "until he had three thousand retainers", turning a result into a time sequence.
issues.suggestion: Read as "so that he had three thousand retainers".

parity_after.overall: The English edition matches the Chinese in facts, dates, numbers, names and quotations throughout; the only discrepancies are minor added glosses in the Hou Ying carriage episode and one causal-to-temporal slip.

edits_applied.before: In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, after Qin had annihilated Zhao's main force at Changping, its armies pressed on and encircled Handan. The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao, but the army never reached the city (retold from the briefing). Instead, envoys from Lord Pingyuan arrived in Daliang one after another — caps of office and carriage canopies in an unbroken line — each message harsher than the last: Handan was within days of surrendering to Qin, and the relief Wei had promised still had not come: was Lord Xinling not the man who prided himself on rushing to others in distress? The last message added a barb: "And have you no pity for your own sister?" Lord Xinling's elder sister was Lord Pingyuan's wife.

edits_applied.before: Start with the sources. The lord's "unease," "self-congratulation," and "blaming himself" are narrative labels, not recorded psychology. edits_applied.before: The other man Lord Xinling honored kept the Yimen — the eastern gate of Daliang. Hou Ying was seventy, poor, and gatekeeper there. Lord Xinling called on him and wanted to make him a handsome gift, but he would not accept: he had "kept himself and his conduct clean for decades," he said, "and would not take the lord's money just because a gatekeeper's life left him poor." So Lord Xinling laid on a feast for his assembled guests, and when everyone was seated he drove out himself with his carriage and escort, leaving the seat of honor at the left of the carriage empty, to fetch Hou Ying in person. The old man turned up in his shabby clothes and worn cap, climbed straight into the seat of honor without yielding it — testing his host — while Lord Xinling held the reins ever more respectfully. At home he seated Hou Ying in the place of honor and introduced him one by one to the assembled guests. The whole company was astonished.

issues.problem: 把「侯生说自己老不能从」放进献计场景。据 SJ0771-E13，「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」是侯生在夷门辞决时说的，不是在此处（E17–E20 的献计与约定）说的；此处唯一与「不能从」相关的安排是 SJ0771-E20「請數公子行日……北鄉自剄，以送公子」。
issues.suggestion: 改为「侯生此前已说过老臣不能从，这里只请数着公子的行程，到晋鄙军那天『北鄉自剄，以送公子』」。

issues.problem: 「用离开把这笔债认下来」把留赵的动机写成史实。SJ0771-E25 只写「使將將其軍歸魏，而公子獨與客留趙」，未写他留赵是为了认债；本段虽标 interpretation，但此句未标「作者推断」，与同稿其他推断的标注方式不一致。
issues.suggestion: 改为「用离开把这笔债认下来（作者推断，原文只写留赵这一行为）」。

issues.problem: 「出城之前，他去向一个看城门的老人告别」与 SJ0771-E13「行過夷門，見侯生……辭決而行」略有出入：原文是他出行途中经过夷门时见侯生，不是出城前专程告别。
issues.suggestion: 改为「出城路上经过夷门，他顺道去看一个看城门的老人，辞决而行」。

issues.problem: 「公子无忌」之名不见于证据包任何一处（SJ0771-E1 至 E25 通称「公子」「魏公子」），属于证据包外信息。

issues.problem: 「侯生自刭的动机……原文只写行为和一句话」表述偏重：SJ0771-E20 明写「北鄉自剄，以送公子」，即原文给出了他自陈的目的（送公子），只是无从核实。
issues.suggestion: 改为「侯生自刭，原文只有一句『以送公子』的自陈，别无交代」。
